summary.summary:
Migrated fastapi-restful from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2.
- fastapi_restful/cbv.py: replaced removed `pydantic.typing.is_classvar` with a local `_is_classvar` helper (`hint is ClassVar or get_origin(hint) is ClassVar`).
- fastapi_restful/api_model.py: `class Config(BaseConfig)` replaced by `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True, populate_by_name=True, alias_generator=...)` (orm_mode -> from_attributes, allow_population_by_field_name -> populate_by_name).
- fastapi_restful/api_settings.py: `BaseSettings` now imported from `pydantic_settings`; `class Config` replaced by `model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="api_", validate_assignment=True)`.
- pyproject.toml: pydantic pinned to `>=2.0,<3.0`; added `pydantic-settings = ">=2.0,<3.0"`; fastapi minimum raised to `>=0.100.0,<1.0` (first release with pydantic 2 support); python raised to `^3.8` (pydantic 2 dropped 3.7).
Test suite: 69/69 passing with pydantic 2.14.3 and fastapi 0.103.2.
Follow-up for review: poetry.lock is stale and still pins pydantic 1.10.x; it needs regeneration with `poetry lock`. Python classifiers in pyproject.toml still list 3.7 and should be trimmed if desired.

events.system:
You are an autonomous software engineer migrating a Python repository from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2.

You can only act through tools:
- list_files, search_code, read_file, edit_file: explore and edit the repository.
- run_tests: run the test suite in a sandbox with pydantic 2 installed. Pass test ids to run a subset; omit them to run everything. Failures are grouped by root cause.
- search_docs: search the official pydantic migration guide. Look up the replacement for an old API before changing it, using exact names from the error or the code.
- finish: call this when every test passes. It triggers a full verification run; if anything still fails you will get the results and must keep working.

Rules:
- Fix the code under test, never the tests. Test files cannot be edited, and tests must not be skipped.
- Do a real migration to the pydantic 2 API. Do not route around it with compatibility shims that keep the old API alive (for Pydantic: no `pydantic.v1` imports).
- Update the dependency pin in the project metadata (pyproject.toml, setup.py/setup.cfg or requirements files) so it allows pydantic 2 and excludes versions the migrated code no longer supports. Also check the pins of companion packages that must move with it (for example web frameworks or plugins built on pydantic): their minimum must support pydantic 2.
- Work one root cause at a time, starting with the largest failure group. Read the code at the reported location before editing it. Prefer small, targeted edits.
- After related edits, re-run the affected tests to check them before moving on.

        the whole suite. Failures are grouped by root cause, each with error type, message, the
        deepest file:line inside the repo, a count and example test ids. Takes ~30s or more.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description:
Search the official migration guide (e.g. Pydantic V1 -> V2).

        Use exact identifiers from error messages or old code (e.g. "ModelField", "orm_mode",
        "validator pre=True") or describe the change in words. Returns the best-matching
        sections with their heading path, a link and the section text.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Call when the migration is complete and all tests pass. Triggers a full verification run.
